learn.title: Why hex exists
learn.body: A byte written in binary is eight digits long, which is hard to read. Hexadecimal, or hex, is a shorter way. It uses base 16, so one hex digit stands for exactly four bits. That means one byte is always two hex digits.

learn.title: The sixteen digits
learn.body: Hex needs 16 symbols. It uses 0 to 9, then letters: A is 10, B is 11, C is 12, D is 13, E is 14 and F is 15. Each place is worth 16 times the one before it: 1, 16, 256 and so on.

learn.title: Reading 0x2F
learn.body: In C, a hex number starts with `0x`. Convert 0x2F to decimal.
steps: Ignore the prefix: the digits are 2 and F
F is 15, and the 2 is in the 16s place

learn.title: Printing hex
learn.body: `%x` prints lowercase hex, `%X` uppercase. `%02x` pads to two digits with a zero. The output is `ff FF 255`, then `0a`.
0xFF is the biggest byte: both hex digits are F. That is 15 * 16 + 15 = 255, the same limit you saw for one byte.

questions.prompt: How many hex digits describe exactly one byte?
questions.explanation: Each hex digit covers 4 bits, so 8 bits need two digits.
